Consider the test class `TestSchemaLoadsCalls` in `marshmallow_qa/schema_loads_m6_calls/files/testcase.py`, run with `pytest marshmallow_qa/schema_loads_m6_calls/files/testcase.py::TestSchemaLoadsCalls` (all of its test methods, in the order pytest collects them; the answer aggregates over ALL of them). Every test method calls `marshmallow.schema.Schema.loads` (file `src/marshmallow/schema.py`) directly, on various `Schema` subclasses.

Scope: every function/method whose `def` statement appears DIRECTLY in the body of class `Schema` in `src/marshmallow/schema.py` (the class named exactly `Schema`, not `SchemaMeta` or `SchemaOpts`, and not any module-level function). This includes `__init__`, dunder methods, classmethods, staticmethods and name-mangled private methods defined there. Excluded: nested functions/closures/lambdas defined inside those methods, comprehension and generator-expression frames, methods of any other class (including the `Schema` subclasses defined in the test file — if a test subclass overrides a method, a call that resolves to the override does NOT count for `Schema`'s version), and functions in other files (e.g. `src/marshmallow/fields.py`, `src/marshmallow/decorators.py`). A call made on a subclass instance that resolves (by inheritance) to the method defined in `Schema`'s body DOES count for that `Schema` method.

Identity: `func` is `marshmallow.schema.` followed by the function's `__qualname__` as Python reports it, e.g. `marshmallow.schema.Schema.some_method` (format example only). Name-mangled methods use their source spelling (the qualname is not mangled), e.g. a method written `def __helper(self)` in the class would be `marshmallow.schema.Schema.__helper`. `file` is the repo-relative path `src/marshmallow/schema.py` for every entry.

Counting: one invocation = one Python `call` event (a new frame created for that function's code object), regardless of who called it (the test, another `Schema` method, field code such as `Nested`/`List`, recursion for `many=True` or nested schemas, decorators' hooks, etc.) and regardless of whether the call returns normally or raises. Recursive/re-entrant calls each count. None of the in-scope functions are generators or coroutines, so no resumption issue arises. Count only calls made while the test methods run (including schema instantiation and any schema classes created lazily during a test, e.g. by `Nested` with a dict); calls during module import / test-module class-body definitions do not count.

Zero rule: every in-scope function appears exactly once in the answer, with `count: 0` if it never ran.

Aggregation: counts are summed across all test methods of the class (whether each method's `loads` call succeeds or raises).

Output: `{"invocation_counts": [{"count": int, "file": str, "func": str}, ...]}`, sorted by `func` ascending using plain Python string ordering (code-point order, so `_` sorts after uppercase letters and before lowercase letters); qualnames are unique, so no tie-break is needed.
